notes: Use a Touch 'n Go card for the LRT and MRT. Grab taxis are cheap (5-15 MYR within the city). The KLIA Ekspres takes 28 minutes and costs 55 MYR.
November to March is monsoon season: short, heavy downpours, so bring an umbrella. Temperatures stay around 30°C all year.
Malaysian food draws on three cultures: nasi lemak (Malay), char kway teow (Chinese) and roti canai (Indian). Mamak restaurants are open 24 hours.
Shoulders and knees must be covered in mosques and Hindu temples. At Batu Caves, monkeys snatch bags.
Petronas Skybridge tickets sell out days ahead. KL Tower is an alternative with a better view.
Alcohol is expensive because of taxes. Tipping is not expected, and a 10% service charge is added.

transit.name: Touch 'n Go Card
transit.why_chosen: Works on the LRT, MRT, monorail and buses. The KLIA Ekspres is separate.
transit.coverage: Rapid KL tüm hatlar, RapidKL otobüs

stops.name: Petronas Twin Towers Skybridge
stops.tips: Skybridge on level 41 plus the level 86 observation deck (~98 MYR). Tickets sell out online days ahead, so book the first morning slot.

stops.name: KLCC Park
stops.tips: Parkland and fountains at the foot of the towers. This is the spot for your photos of them.

stops.name: Nasi Lemak Wanjo Kampung Baru
stops.tips: A Kampung Baru nasi lemak classic with sambal and chicken, within walking distance of KLCC.

stops.name: Kampung Baru
stops.tips: A Malay village in the middle of the skyscrapers, with wooden houses and street stalls.

stops.name: KL Tower Sky Deck
stops.tips: The glass box at Menara KL and the sunset. It's the best place to see the Petronas Towers from across the city.

backups.name: Suria KLCC Signatures Food Court
backups.tips: Mall food court with laksa and satay.

backups.name: Aquaria KLCC
backups.tips: An aquarium beneath the convention centre. A good rainy-day option.

stops.name: Batu Caves
stops.tips: 30 minutes by KTM train. Climb 272 colourful steps to the giant Murugan statue, and watch out for the monkeys. The morning is cool and quiet.

stops.name: Petaling Street
stops.tips: Chinatown market with fake designer bags and street food. Haggle.

stops.name: Hong Kee Claypot Chicken Rice
stops.tips: Claypot rice cooked over charcoal on Petaling Street. Expect a lunchtime queue.

stops.name: Sri Mahamariamman Temple
stops.tips: KL's oldest Hindu temple, with a colourful gopuram (gateway tower).

stops.name: Central Market Kuala Lumpur
stops.tips: An art deco market with batik and handicrafts, and it's air-conditioned.

backups.name: Kim Lian Kee Hokkien Mee
backups.tips: Hokkien mee since 1927, on Petaling Street.

stops.name: Merdeka Square
stops.tips: Independence Square and the Sultan Abdul Samad Building, best in the morning light.

stops.name: Masjid Jamek
stops.tips: A Moorish-style mosque where two rivers meet. Outside visiting hours, admire it from the outside.

stops.name: River of Life Walk
stops.tips: A restored riverside walkway along the Klang River, with blue-lit fountains.

stops.name: Islamic Arts Museum Malaysia
stops.tips: Asia's best Islamic art museum, air-conditioned, with domes and calligraphy.

stops.name: Jalan Alor
stops.tips: Bukit Bintang's street food strip: grilled seafood, satay and char kway teow. It comes alive in the evening.

backups.name: Pavilion KL Food Court
backups.tips: Food court in the Bukit Bintang mall. A good rainy-day option.

backups.name: Perdana Botanical Garden
backups.tips: The city's botanical park, with an orchid garden. An alternative to the museum.

stops.name: Brickfields Little India
stops.tips: A colourful Indian neighbourhood with temples and flower garlands.

stops.name: Thean Hou Temple
stops.tips: A six-tier Chinese temple on a hilltop, with red lanterns and city views.

stops.name: Vishal Food & Catering Brickfields
stops.tips: South Indian food served on a banana leaf. Eat with your hands.

stops.name: Bangsar Village
stops.tips: A stylish neighbourhood with cafes and boutiques.

stops.name: Bangsar Devi's Corner
stops.tips: Roti canai and teh tarik (pulled milk tea) at a 24-hour mamak.

backups.name: National Museum
backups.tips: The national museum, covering Malaysian history. Good in the rain.

stops.name: Dutch Square Melaka
stops.tips: 2 hours from KL by bus (~15 MYR). See the red Stadthuys and Christ Church, a UNESCO site.

stops.name: A Famosa
stops.tips: The Portuguese fortress gate and St. Paul's Hill, with views over the Strait of Malacca.

stops.name: Jonker Street
stops.tips: Peranakan antique shops and cafes, plus a night market at weekends.

stops.name: Hoe Kee Chicken Rice Ball
stops.tips: Melaka's chicken rice with rice shaped into balls. The queue moves fast.

stops.name: Baba & Nyonya Heritage Museum
stops.tips: A Peranakan townhouse, visited on a guided tour.

backups.name: Nancy's Kitchen Melaka
backups.tips: Nyonya cooking, including ayam pongteh (chicken and potato stew).

backups.name: Melaka River Cruise
backups.tips: A river boat ride. An alternative to the museum.

stops.name: Kuala Selangor Sky Mirror
stops.tips: A mirror-like sandbar that appears at low tide (depends on the lunar calendar, tour ~120 MYR). Malaysia's Uyuni.

stops.name: Kuala Selangor Seafood Restaurant
stops.tips: Fishing-village seafood at Pasir Penambang.

stops.name: Bukit Melawati
stops.tips: Hilltop fort ruins and silvered leaf monkeys.

stops.name: Kuala Selangor Fireflies Tour
stops.tips: A boat trip through the mangroves at Kampung Kuantan. Watch the fireflies in the dark.

backups.name: Sekinchan Rice Fields
backups.tips: Rice fields near Kuala Selangor, best in harvest season.

days.theme: Temple morning and a gentle farewell

stops.name: Masjid Negara
stops.tips: The National Mosque, with a blue star-shaped dome. Robes are provided during visiting hours.

stops.name: Kuala Lumpur Railway Station
stops.tips: A historic Moorish-style station. Good for photos.

stops.name: Restoran Yut Kee
stops.tips: Hainanese coffee and roti babi since 1928. A fitting farewell lunch.

stops.name: KL Sentral
stops.tips: The KLIA Ekspres takes 28 minutes. Time to say goodbye.

backups.name: KL Bird Park
backups.tips: The world's largest free-flight walk-in aviary. An alternative to the mosque.
